title: Ohio Chamber sues healthcare giant, accusing it of deceit, misinformation
summary: The Ohio Chamber of Commerce has filed a lawsuit against UnitedHealth, alleging that the healthcare giant breached its contract to administer a Chamber-backed health plan. The lawsuit claims UnitedHealth used inside information and Chamber branding to divert participating employers to its own insurance offerings, confusing them into believing United's products were Chamber-approved. The Chamber is seeking an injunction and compensatory and punitive damages for alleged deceptive trade practices, false advertising, and breach of contract.

title: Puma Biotechnology initiates phase II lung cancer trial

This trial follows previous initiations for alisertib monotherapy and combination therapy in other cancer types.

title: Phase 3 Pediatric EMPAVELI Data Published in Clinical Journal of the American Society of Nephrology Show Reduction in Proteinuria and Stabilized Kidney Function in Adolescents with C3G or Primary IC-MPGN
summary: Biogen announced the publication of Phase 3 VALIANT study data in the Clinical Journal of the American Society of Nephrology, showing that EMPAVELI significantly reduced proteinuria and stabilized kidney function in adolescents aged 12-17 with C3G or primary IC-MPGN. This publication supports EMPAVELI as the only approved treatment for these conditions in adolescents, following a recent FDA label expansion. The results highlight EMPAVELI's potential to prevent progressive kidney damage and the need for kidney transplants in young patients.

title: Old El Paso: From local cannery to General Mills company
summary: The article traces the history of the Old El Paso brand from its origins as Mountain Pass Canning and Valley Canning Co. in the Borderland region. Dick, through several corporate acquisitions by companies like Pet Inc., Pillsbury Co., and eventually General Mills, which led to the closure of its original canning factory in Anthony, Texas.

title: Old El Paso: From local cannery to General Mills company
summary: The Old El Paso brand, known for its Mexican food products, originated in the Borderland region from local canneries. Co-founded by Tom Barwise and James A. Dick, the brand grew from Mountain Pass Canning and Valley Canning Co., eventually being acquired by General Mills in 2001. Despite its national success, the original canning factory in Anthony, Texas, closed in 2002, ending local production.
